ai_assessment.method: Full direct French-to-Vietnamese comparison of all 128 canonical paragraphs and both titles. A separate-context assessor (same model family, not shown the drafter’s notes or scores) read every pair first and reported 1 major and 18 minor findings with a pre-revision weighted score of 8.725; the drafter revised the text, then re-read the changed passages and the whole target aloud-style for naturalness before assigning these final scores, bound to the final byte hashes.
ai_assessment.limitations: The same AI system drafted, revised and assessed the work; the separate-context pass is correlated same-model feedback, not independent review or model diversity. No human literary reviewer, native-reader trial or measured reader demand is claimed. Existing Vietnamese translations were not consulted or collated. Scores are subjective and uncalibrated; missed errors may remain. Source clearance is separately recorded and is not granted by this review.

findings.explanation: The narrator’s reflection had used slangy tiêu đời and a stiff adjectival đổi thay. Revised to “Đời sao mà kỳ lạ, mà đổi thay khôn lường! Chỉ cần một chút cỏn con là đủ khiến ta mất tất cả hay cứu vớt được ta!”, restoring gravity and the echo between losing the necklace and being lost.

Changed the draft title Chuỗi vòng cổ, which doubled two necklace words and matched neither body term, to Món trang sức, which keeps the generic sense of parure and links to passages 1.2, 1.45, 1.91, 1.96 and 1.106.
Parure rendered as món trang sức here and in 1.96 and 1.106 instead of the uncommon chuỗi vòng.
Replaced khoái lạc, which leans carnal in Vietnamese, with niềm vui thú for grisée par le plaisir.
Restored the deliberate polysyndeton of la femme forte, et dure, et rude; rendered si fêtée as được tung hô, săn đón and cette soirée as buổi dạ hội for term consistency.
Replaced the potentially inclusive bọn mình with vợ chồng mình so Mme Forestier is not grammatically included among those who paid.
Cette bourgeoise means an ordinary woman of modest condition; replaced xuềnh xoàng (slovenly) with bình dân, echoing femme du peuple in 1.100.
Avec dépit is vexation, not hostility: hằn học changed to bực dọc.
S’enfuit avec son trésor restored as chạy biến đi, keeping the hint of flight with a prize.
Removed an added cũng so the short final sentence about the minister keeps its weight.
Replaced repeated khủng khiếp (horrible / effroyable) with cùng cực and kinh khủng, and the ill-fitting connective vả lại with vả chăng.
Ma chère no longer calqued as bạn thân mến: “Cậu cứ chọn đi, bạn yêu.”
Đạm bạc describes meals; son humble ménage is now những việc nhà lặt vặt.
Applied the witness’s lowercase after internal ? and ! consistently (1.4, 1.19, 1.68), matching 1.98, 1.106 and 2.12.
Restored the emphatic à moi as Anh thì thấy.
Nồi thịt hầm keeps the homely tureen dish but not the culturally specific name pot-au-feu; a loanword would be more exact and less legible.
Nàng gives Mathilde a literary narrative register that persists after her hardening (1.99–1.105). The ironic distance is defensible, but some readers may prefer a shift to chị in the second half.
Tuyên bố for déclarer remains slightly formal in domestic speech at 1.4 and 1.88; it is kept where the mock-solemn irony supports it.

summary: Full assessment of all 128 French/Vietnamese paragraphs and both titles. Every proposition, sum of money, place, date and dialogue turn is present, from Mathilde’s dreams and the invitation through the borrowed necklace, the ball, the loss, the 36,000-franc replacement, ten years of debt and the final revelation that the original was paste. The address system (nàng/anh/bà; anh/em; mình/cậu, then tôi/bà at non-recognition) is consistent. The one major register defect in the narrator’s reflection (1.106) and the weak draft title were revised; parure, rivière, fête, soirée and bal now map to stable Vietnamese terms. Fidelity, imagery and mechanics are 9.0; voice and naturalness 8.5 because the nàng register, some formal reporting verbs and the pot-au-feu substitution are imperfect equivalents. Unrounded weighted score 8.8 meets the unchanged 8.6 threshold. No unresolved major or critical issue remains. Same-system drafting, revision and assessment are disclosed; no human approval is claimed.

title_review.rationale: La Parure names an adornment rather than specifically a necklace. Món trang sức keeps that generic sense and links the title to Mathilde’s inability to adorn herself (1.2), the jewels she tries on (1.45) and the object she loses and repays (1.91, 1.96, 1.106). It does not reveal the diamonds or their falseness. Familiar Vietnamese titles such as Chuỗi hạt kim cương or Sợi dây chuyền are more recognisable but narrower; this edition prefers the source’s generality.
